blocks.text: Himadri Speciality Chemical (HSCL) is, at its economic core, a coal tar distiller. It buys coal tar, a by-product of steel-plant coke ovens, and splits it into coal tar pitch (sold to aluminium smelters and graphite electrode makers), carbon black feedstock oil, naphthalene and speciality oils [F] (AR2026 p.99, p.126). About one-third of output is consumed internally [F] (AR2026 p.126), mainly to make carbon black (250,000 MTPA, of which 130,000 MTPA is speciality grade) and naphthalene derivatives such as SNF/PCE concrete admixtures [F] (AR2026 p.81, p.78). Around this core sit three newer layers: (i) Birla Tyres, a revived insolvent tyre maker that management says generated Rs 187 cr of revenue in FY26 [MC] (CALL May 2026); (ii) speciality chemicals under construction (anthraquinone/carbazole, carbon nanotubes, super-speciality carbon black) [F] (PPT Jul 2026); and (iii) battery materials (a 200 MTPA anode plant commissioned 23 April 2026 and a 2,000 MTPA LFP cathode demo line targeted for Q3FY27) [F] (AR2026 p.437) [MC] (CALL Jul 2026).

**How it makes money.** Raw-material prices are passed through to customers through predefined formulas [MC] (AR2026 p.126), so profit is a spread per tonne, not a function of price. Standalone EBITDA per tonne was about Rs 17,300 in FY26 [E] (AR2026 p.129; PPT Jul 2026 volume 564,206 t) and Rs 22,857 in Q1FY27 [E] (PPT Jul 2026). Long-term contracts make up about one-third of sales [MC] (AR2026 p.126).

The standalone BRSR gives 31.54% exports across 61 countries [F] (AR2026 p.225). **Customer profile.** Customers are B2B industrial buyers. The top customer was 9% of consolidated revenue (FY25: 10%) and the top five were 32% (FY25: 41%) [F] (AR2026 p.511). No customer is named anywhere in the documents.

The evidence base is therefore a full annual report and four earnings calls, not a prospectus, and no offer document was available. The ICRA rating rationale in the folder was not readable (paywalled page), so rating facts come from the annual report only [F] (RATING) (AR2026 p.193).

blocks.text: Classification [AI]: theses 1 and 7 are **structural** (permitting barriers, smelter qualification, aluminium capacity growth). Theses 2, 3 and 6 are **company-specific** (own R&D, mix shift, feedstock integration). Thesis 4 is company-specific but **cyclical** in its funding capacity, because carbon black and pitch spreads are cyclical. Thesis 5 is company-specific optionality that rides a structural theme (energy transition) but has no revenue yet.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. **Valuation requires a different company.** The reverse DCF implies about 70% annual sales growth for five years against an 8.3% base-case equivalent. All three DCF cases (Rs 65, 109 and 145 per share) sit 78-90% below the Rs 665 price [F] (NUMBERS).

2. **Top line has been flat for four years.** Sales were Rs 4,172 cr in FY23 and Rs 4,661 cr in FY26, a 3.8% 3-year CAGR [F] (NUMBERS). Management concedes it has not seen top-line growth for 3-4 years [MC] (CALL May 2026). Standalone volume fell 5.9% year on year in Q1FY27 [E] (PPT Jul 2026).

3. **Cash conversion is deteriorating.** CFO/PAT was 0.51x in FY26 and 0.72x over three years [F] (NUMBERS). FY26 working capital absorbed Rs 370 cr, with raw-material inventory nearly doubling to Rs 416 cr [F] (AR2026 p.453, p.476). FCF was negative at Rs -63 cr [F] (NUMBERS).

4. **Profit growth is flattered by non-operating items.** Other income was Rs 171 cr (17% of PBT), including a Rs 100 cr fair-value gain on unlisted investments [F] (AR2026 p.490) (NUMBERS). The switch to the s.115BAA tax regime cut the effective tax rate from 31.1% to 24.6% [F] (AR2026 p.494). Excluding both, FY26 PAT growth would be about 11% rather than 36% [E].

5. **Rs 487 cr is parked in 0.001% NCDs of Dalmia Bharat Refractories,** Himadri's co-acquirer of Birla Tyres. The holding rose from Rs 187 cr and is valued at Level 2 [F] (AR2026 p.468, p.506). Management says Birla Tyres economics sit on the Dalmia Refractories balance sheet and are not yet consolidated [MC] (CALL Jul 2026). This is a large, near-zero-yield, opaque exposure to an unconsolidated tyre turnaround.

6. **Promoter-entity investment.** HSCL holds Rs 182.6 cr of 1% non-cumulative optionally convertible preference shares in Modern Hi-Rise, its 36.75% promoter shareholder, with a 20-year life from 2019 [F] (AR2026 p.469, p.478). It also pays Rs 14.4 cr a year in rent to a KMP-controlled company [F] (AR2026 p.501).

7. **Battery timelines have slipped and are being redefined.** In Oct 2025 a 40,000 MTPA LFP plant was to start operations by Q3FY27 [MC] (CALL Oct 2025). By Jul 2026, Q3FY27 is a 2,000 MTPA demo line and the 40,000 MTPA is 'operational in FY28' with full operations in FY29 [MC] (CALL May 2026) (CALL Jul 2026). No offtake is disclosed (NDAs cited) [MC] (CALL May 2026).

8. **Capex outruns internal cash.** About Rs 1,000 cr of capex a year is planned for FY27 and FY28 [MC] (CALL Jul 2026), against FY26 CFO of Rs 382 cr [F] (NUMBERS). Management says no incremental debt will be needed [MC] (CALL Jul 2026); the arithmetic does not support that without a sharp CFO recovery [AI].

9. **Disclosure is thin where it matters.** There is no product-wise revenue, no plant utilisation in the annual report, no margin guidance for new businesses, anode capex not announced, LFP customers unnamed and the LFP spread not explained ('I cannot disclose my sources') [MC] (CALL Jul 2026) (AR2026 p.86).

10. **Cyclical and environmental exposure.** The business depends on aluminium, graphite and tyre demand and on steel-industry coal tar supply [F] (AR2026 p.110, p.126). A 10% input-cost shock that is not passed through would cut FY26 EBITDA by about 30% [E] (see raw materials section).

**Is the 21% EBITDA margin structural?** Bull: yield, waste-heat and mix improvements are claimed as permanent, with 65-70% of the gain attributed to mix [MC] (CALL Oct 2025). Bear: the margin step-up coincided with falling raw-material prices (average RM Rs 39,500/t vs Rs 45,000/t) [MC] (CALL Oct 2025), and a pass-through model raises margin % when prices fall [AI]. The Q1FY27 realisation jump (+23%/t) came with higher input prices and margins held [E] (PPT Jul 2026), which modestly supports the bull side.

**Is the market paying for battery materials that do not yet exist?** Our view [AI] is yes. Price/book of 7.1x and P/E of 41.7x [F] (NUMBERS) are hard to reconcile with a coal-tar business growing sales at 4% a year. The market may be underestimating execution risk and how far the timelines have moved [AI].

**Is the Birla Tyres structure a hidden liability or hidden value?** Birla Tyres revenue runs through Himadri Clean Energy as a trading business (HCEL turnover Rs 187.6 cr, PAT Rs 4.0 cr) [F] (AR2026 p.145), while manufacturing sits at DBRL, which HSCL funds through NCDs [MC] (CALL Jan 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.468). The market may be missing both the funding drain (Rs 300 cr of new NCDs in FY26) and the possibility of a cheap asset (bought at about 10% of replacement value) [MC] (AR2026 p.74).

**Is other income sustainable?** Management guides that other income will 'vary 30% to 40% quarter-on-quarter' [MC] (CALL Jul 2026). Part of it is treasury carry on bank borrowings redeposited at higher rates [MC] (CALL May 2026), and part is unrealised mark-ups on IBC, Sicona and DBRL instruments [F] (AR2026 p.490). On our reading the market treats it as recurring; it is not [AI].

blocks.text: Our variant view [AI] is that the market prices HSCL as a battery-materials growth company, while the reported numbers describe a well-run, cash-hungry coal tar and carbon black processor. That business has expanded margins impressively but has not grown volumes or revenue meaningfully since FY23 (NUMBERS) (PPT Jul 2026). Its FY26 profit growth was boosted by tax, fair-value and treasury items (AR2026 p.490, p.494). Its balance sheet increasingly holds financial claims on related or quasi-related counterparties (DBRL NCDs, Modern Hi-Rise OCPS, loans to subsidiaries) rather than operating assets (AR2026 p.468-469, p.390). The core franchise is genuine and well protected. The debate is not whether HSCL is a good business; it is whether a 70% implied sales CAGR (NUMBERS) is a sensible price for options whose commissioning dates have already moved.

The group made the investments in Sicona (Australia), IBC (USA) and DBRL directly, as financial instruments rather than subsidiaries [F] (AR2026 p.468).

The coal tar business is 35 years old, and the carbon black business dates from 2010-2014 [F] (AR2026 p.28). Everything in the growth narrative is very recent [AI]: tyres from FY26, the 130,000 MTPA speciality carbon black line from Feb 2026, anode from April 2026, and LFP, CNT and anthraquinone/carbazole still to come (AR2026 p.134, p.437) (PPT Jul 2026). Six subsidiaries were added in FY26 alone [F] (AR2026 p.132). In other words, the earning base is old and the narrative base is less than 18 months old [AI]. The recent pace of entity creation (tyres, logistics, minerals, agro, new energy) also widens the related-party and control surface that investors need to monitor [AI].

items: Step 1, feedstock: coal tar is bought from coke ovens of steel plants under long-term relationships. Distillation plants sit next to steel makers [F] (AR2026 p.85, p.126). Some coal tar and oils are sourced overseas, including through AAT Global, which sold Rs 328.5 cr of raw material to HSCL in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.420).
Step 2, distillation: 600,000 TPA of coal tar distillation across eight dispersed plants plus Mahistikry [F] (AR2026 p.85-86).
Step 3, primary products: coal tar pitch (including zero-QI and liquid pitch), carbon black feedstock oil, naphthalene and speciality oils [F] (AR2026 p.86-87).

Step 4, captive conversion: about one-third of output is used internally [F] (AR2026 p.126). Oil goes to carbon black (250,000 MTPA), naphthalene to SNF/PCE and Durofresh mothballs, and pitch to anode precursor [F] (AR2026 p.81, p.88) [MC] (CALL May 2026).
Step 5, energy: waste-heat recovery powers a 28-32 MW captive plant that supplies 100% of electricity needs; surplus power is sold [F] (AR2026 p.94, p.312).

Step 6, logistics: 292 heated tankers deliver molten pitch; liquid pitch is exported through the Haldia and Mangalore terminals [F] (AR2026 p.86). A Rs 124 cr security deposit has been placed with a transport provider for a dedicated tanker fleet [F] (AR2026 p.392).

Step 7, downstream new lines: anode (200 MTPA), LFP (2,000 MTPA demo), anthraquinone/carbazole, CNT and SSCB [F] (PPT Jul 2026). Tyres are a separate chain that consumes the group's own carbon black [MC] (AR2026 p.69).

blocks.text: Value is captured in three places [AI]. First, in converting a low-value by-product into qualified pitch that smelters cannot easily requalify, which is a switching-cost spread. Second, in using captive oil for carbon black, where management claims consistency and yield advantages over petroleum-based feedstock [MC] (CALL Oct 2025). Third, in the waste-heat power credit. In FY26 the carbon segment earned a 19.0% result margin and power earned Rs 81 cr, mostly on inter-segment sales [E] (AR2026 p.503). Note that the power segment result is an internal transfer-price construct [AI].

The legacy business is capital-light at the margin. Fixed-asset turnover was 2.4-2.9x over FY23-FY26, and capex averaged 1.3-3.7% of sales over FY23-FY25 before jumping to 9.5% in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS). New businesses are heavier. LFP needs Rs 1,125 cr for 40,000 MTPA with an asset turn of about 2x claimed [MC] (CALL May 2026), and Rs 4,800 cr for 200,000 MTPA [MC] (CALL Jul 2026). That Rs 4,800 cr is close to total FY26 equity of Rs 4,706 cr [E] (NUMBERS). Logistics is partly outsourced (dedicated tanker fleet on a deposit model) [F] (AR2026 p.392). Tyre manufacturing is effectively outsourced to DBRL for now [MC] (CALL Jan 2026).

blocks.text: Commodity-like [AI]: rubber carbon black, SNF/PCE, naphthalene, power, and to an extent bulk pitch on price. Differentiated [AI]: qualified smelter pitch (switching cost rather than product uniqueness), zero-QI and liquid pitch, and speciality carbon black grades. Unproven [AI]: anode, LFP, CNT and SSCB. Speciality carbon black is the swing factor because it doubled in capacity in Feb 2026 (AR2026 p.134). Its margin is not disclosed separately, so the mix shift can only be inferred from blended EBITDA per tonne [AI].

Source: [F] (AR2026 p.503-505). FY24 segment data is not in the documents available, so we show only two years. Segment results are disclosed, but they are before other income, finance cost and FX [F] (AR2026 p.503). The 'Others' segment was new in FY26 and, per management, includes tyres and mining [MC] (CALL May 2026). The consolidated P&L shows Rs 197.7 cr of 'purchase of trading goods' in FY26 against nil in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.448). This is consistent with HCEL buying Birla tyres from DBRL for resale [AI].

items: Carbon materials: revenue fell 4.8% while the result rose 18.5% [E] (AR2026 p.503). Management attributes the revenue fall to lower raw-material-linked prices and an export cargo deferred from Q2 to Q3 [MC] (CALL Oct 2025), and the margin gain to mix (65-70%) and efficiency (30%) [MC] (CALL Oct 2025). Our read [AI]: with volumes up only 2.2% (552,206 t to 564,206 t) [E] (PPT Jul 2026), almost all profit growth came from spread per tonne. That spread is partly mechanical, because a pass-through model with stable absolute margins raises margin % when prices fall.
Power: down as internal demand rose [AI]; no management explanation was found.

Others: Q4FY26 'Others' EBIT was about Rs 25 cr, falling to about Rs 1 cr in Q1FY27 because mining did not operate pending licensing and environmental clearance [MC] (CALL Jul 2026). Mining in this segment is not described anywhere in the annual report beyond 'mining and other business' [F] (AR2026 p.503). **The nature, location and ownership of the mining operation are not disclosed**, which is a disclosure gap [AI].

blocks.text: Order-driven vs organic [AI]: none of the segments is order-book driven. Carbon materials is volume and spread driven under formula contracts, about one-third long-term [MC] (AR2026 p.126). Tyres are distribution driven. Battery materials will become qualification-and-offtake driven, with no offtake disclosed yet.

sections.title: Exports, domestic mix and trade exposure

blocks.text: Source: [F] (AR2026 p.505). A longer series and a country split are not disclosed, so no multi-year CAGR can be computed. Exports go to 61 countries (56 the year before) [MC] (CALL May 2026) [F] (AR2026 p.25). Standalone foreign exchange earnings were Rs 1,048 cr against outgo of Rs 809 cr in FY26 (FY25: Rs 811 cr and Rs 940 cr) [F] (AR2026 p.158). Coal tar division exports are 20%, with a 2030 target of 50% [MC] (AR2026 p.113).

The export rise looks partly strategic: dedicated liquid-pitch terminals and Middle East smelter approvals [MC] (CALL Oct 2025). It is also partly circumstantial, because domestic revenue fell with pass-through prices [AI]. Management's focus for pitch is the Middle East, not Europe [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). The West Asia conflict forced some cargoes to be diverted to Southeast Asia and Africa [MC] (CALL May 2026).

items: Currency: the policy is to leave positions open because exports and imports are 'more or less in parity' [MC] (CALL May 2026). Yet HSCL booked FX losses of Rs 43.6 cr in FY26 and Rs 25.2 cr in Q1FY27 after hedging during volatility [F] (PPT Jul 2026). Net unhedged exposure at FY26 was Rs 363 cr consolidated, mainly USD Rs 165 cr and AUD Rs 159 cr (Sicona) [F] (AR2026 p.513).

Tariffs: management said US tariffs had 'no impact' in Q2FY26 because of geographic diversification [MC] (CALL Oct 2025). A nearly 160% US tariff on Chinese graphite anode material is presented as an opportunity [MC] (AR2026 p.118). No dated tariff exposure is quantified [AI].

Single-location risk: Mahistikry hosts the flagship distillation complex, all 130,000 MTPA of speciality carbon black, the anode plant and the R&D centre [F] (AR2026 p.78, p.85). This is a material concentration of earnings in one site [AI]. Other distillation plants are dispersed [F] (AR2026 p.85).

The key input is coal tar, a steel coke-oven by-product bought from co-located steel plants on long-term relationships [F] (AR2026 p.126). Carbon black also uses some petroleum-based oil [MC] (CALL Oct 2025). The LFP inputs (lithium carbonate, iron phosphate) will come from Latin America, Australia and China [MC] (CALL Jan 2026). Inputs sourced within India were 83.30% in FY26 vs 78.17% in FY25 [F] (AR2026 p.336), so imported inputs were about 16.7% vs 21.8% [E]. The country split is not disclosed. Standalone foreign exchange outgo was Rs 809 cr (FY25 Rs 940 cr), including capital goods [F] (AR2026 p.158).

The average raw-material price fell from about Rs 45,000/t to Rs 39,500/t between Q2FY25 and Q2FY26 [MC] (CALL Oct 2025). Raw-material prices rose again into Q1FY27 [MC] (CALL Jul 2026). Management claims '100%' pass-through, so price moves change margin % and top line but not absolute margin [MC] (CALL Oct 2025). Evidence for this: absolute standalone EBITDA per tonne rose in both the falling-price period (FY26) and the rising-price quarter (Q1FY27) [E] (PPT Jul 2026), which is consistent with pass-through plus mix. Evidence against: the standalone 'variable consideration' adjustment swung from +Rs 42.4 cr to -Rs 55.6 cr [F] (AR2026 p.405), showing that price adjustments to customers are material and judgmental (also the key audit matter) [F] (AR2026 p.353). A further concern is that a pass-through model does not protect volumes [AI].

blocks.text: Illustrative arithmetic only [E]. HSCL's FY26 consolidated revenue of Rs 4,661 cr [F] (NUMBERS) is a small fraction of these markets. The planned 40,000 MTPA of LFP would be about 2.5% of today's stated 1.6 Mn t LFP market [E], and 200,000 MTPA would be about 12.5% of today's market. Management itself says it is targeting 2-3% of a future market [MC] (CALL Jul 2026). The planned 6,000 MTPA of SSCB would be about 2% of a 300,000 t market [E]. None of these shares is evidenced by contracts, so the percentages describe capacity, not demand captured [AI]. The 700-800 kt figure for incremental Indian pitch demand looks implausibly large relative to HSCL's whole 600,000 t distillation capacity [AI]. It is a company estimate and has not been verified.

A bottom-up frame is more useful [AI]: about 560,000 t of standalone volume a year (PPT Jul 2026), multiplied by EBITDA of Rs 17,000-23,000 per tonne (CALL May 2026; our estimate above), gives a core EBITDA range of roughly Rs 950-1,300 cr at current volume [E]. On top of that sit the new businesses, each with company-stated revenue potential but no disclosed margins (CALL Jul 2026).

Indian pitch is concentrated, with HSCL claiming about 65% [MC] (AR2026 p.87), and sold directly to smelters. Carbon black is an oligopoly of global multinationals plus Indian players, sold direct to tyre and industrial customers. Only 6.88% of standalone sales go through 18 dealers [F] (AR2026 p.260). Tyres sell through distributors and dealers [MC] (PPT Jul 2026). LFP is concentrated in China and sold direct to cell makers [MC] (CALL Jul 2026).

It is generous in two respects [AI]: it assumes growth accelerates to 10% (base) or 13% (bull) by year 5 despite a flat four-year top line; and its asset-turnover capex rule implies less capex than the Rs 2,000 cr management has guided [MC] (CALL Jul 2026).
Even allowing for the conservative items, the distance to the price (-78% to -90%) is too large to be closed by adjusting inputs within any reasonable range [F] (NUMBERS) [AI].

blocks.text: At the base margin, WACC and terminal growth, today's EV requires about **70.2% annual sales growth for five years**. The base case's equivalent constant growth is 8.3% [F] (NUMBERS). For comparison, HSCL's sales CAGR was 3.8% over three years, 22.7% over five years (from the FY21 trough) and 14.8% over nine years [F] (NUMBERS). The bull case assumes 12-13% [F] (NUMBERS).

The price is not a valuation of the business that exists [AI]. It assumes the battery-materials, tyre and speciality programmes reach management's aspirational scale (LFP Rs 3,000 cr at Phase 1, Rs 30,000 cr of Li-ion revenue, Birla Tyres Rs 3,000 cr) [MC] (CALL Jul 2026) at margins at least as good as today's. None of these has a disclosed contract, and the LFP timeline has already been re-scoped once (CALL Oct 2025) (CALL Jul 2026).

For balance [AI]: a generic DCF with a 14.9% WACC will always undervalue a company in the middle of a step-change in its asset base. HSCL has already compounded EBITDA at 34% a year over three years [F] (NUMBERS) and met its own PAT target a year early on a TTM basis [E] (NUMBERS). If the LFP economics claimed by management prove out (about 2x asset turn, a 30% ROCE hurdle) [MC] (CALL May 2026) (AR2026 p.90), and the 200,000 MTPA roadmap is funded and built, revenue could rise several-fold within the model horizon. blocks.text: HSCL owns a protected, cash-generative coal tar franchise with about 65% domestic pitch share [MC] (AR2026 p.87). It has tripled EBITDA in four years with little capex [F] (NUMBERS) and has just doubled speciality carbon black capacity (AR2026 p.134). Its balance sheet carries gross cash roughly equal to debt (AR2026 p.517). Management has hit its own profit targets early [MC] (CALL Jan 2026) and is building a portfolio of options (LFP, anode, CNT, AQ/carbazole, tyres) that could transform the revenue base [MC] (CALL Jul 2026).

Revenue has been flat for four years and Q1FY27 volumes fell [F] (NUMBERS) (PPT Jul 2026). FY26 profit growth was flattered by fair-value gains and tax (AR2026 p.490, p.494). Cash conversion is deteriorating (NUMBERS). The balance sheet is accumulating large, low-yield exposures to a tyre co-investor and a promoter holding company (AR2026 p.468-469). The battery timelines have been re-scoped (CALL Oct 2025) (CALL Jul 2026). The price requires about 70% annual sales growth (NUMBERS).

items: Downside [AI]: the off-balance-sheet tyre structure and its Rs 486.5 cr of NCD funding; the non-operating share of PAT; the cash needs of the capex plan.

Upside [AI]: per-tonne economics in the core are still rising (Q1FY27 about Rs 22,900/t) [E], and an 80% to 90%+ distillation utilisation ramp plus speciality CB could lift core EBITDA without any battery revenue.

blocks.text: In five years [AI], HSCL could plausibly be either (a) a larger, higher-margin carbon materials company with some tyres and speciality chemicals, or (b) a genuine non-Chinese battery-materials supplier with LFP at 40,000 MTPA or more. Our DCF captures the first. The share price discounts something closer to the second at full scale (NUMBERS). The documents give evidence that (a) is under way and only plans and samples for (b) (CALL Jul 2026).

subsections.title: Research view (no rating, no price target)

blocks.text: The share price of Rs 665 sits 4.6x above the bull-case value (Rs 145.4), 6.1x above the base (Rs 108.9) and about 10x above the bear (Rs 64.8) in our DCF [F] (NUMBERS) [E]. The gap is driven almost entirely by the market capitalising battery-materials and tyre aspirations that have no disclosed contracts [AI]. A secondary driver is a PAT figure about one-fifth of which is non-operating [AI]. Discount-rate choices do not explain it: the most favourable sensitivity cell is Rs 145.5 [F] (NUMBERS). The underlying coal tar and carbon black business is solid and improving, but on our evidence it is not a growth business at the rate implied [AI].

Horizon and re-review [AI]. This is a thesis to be tested over 12-24 months against hard milestones, not a near-term call. Re-review points: (1) Q2FY27 results (Oct 2026) for volumes, FX and AQ/carbazole commissioning; (2) Q3FY27 results (Jan 2027) for the LFP demo line and Birla Tyres breakeven; (3) the FY27 annual report (mid-2027) for DBRL NCDs, fair-value detail and subsidiary results; (4) any exchange filing on anode capex or LFP offtake.

This is our initial coverage of Himadri Speciality Chemical. No previous report exists, so there is no prior-quarter baseline for numbers, guidance delivery, risks or thesis. The guidance tracker in this report tests earlier management call guidance (Oct 2025 to Jul 2026) against the latest reported figures, and the summary records this quarter's guidance items for next quarter's tracker.

summary.one_line: Himadri is a well-protected, margin-improving coal tar and carbon black processor whose flat revenue, weakening cash conversion, non-operating profit boost and large quasi-related financial exposures sit uneasily with a share price that our DCF shows requires about 70% annual sales growth, more than four times even the bull-case value.
bull_points: [MC] About 65% domestic coal tar pitch share, with smelters relaxing supplier caps for HSCL and a claimed record of never losing a customer, in a permit-protected industry (AR2026 p.86-87, p.113).
[F] EBITDA rose from Rs 156 cr (FY22) to Rs 962 cr (FY26), and the margin from 5.6% to 20.6%, with cumulative FY24-FY26 capex of only Rs 669 cr (NUMBERS).

[E] Standalone EBITDA per tonne rose from about Rs 16,700 in Q1FY26 to about Rs 22,900 in Q1FY27 as 70,000 MTPA of new speciality carbon black capacity started commercial operation (PPT Jul 2026; AR2026 p.134).
[F] Low leverage: debt/equity 0.16, interest cover 16.6x, and gross cash, bank and mutual funds of Rs 860 cr against borrowings of Rs 767 cr (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.517).
[MC] Multiple new lines under construction (AQ/carbazole Q2FY27, LFP 2,000 MTPA Q3FY27, CNT Q4FY27, SSCB Q4FY28), with a reaffirmed FY28 PAT target of Rs 1,100 cr+ (CALL Jul 2026; PPT Jul 2026).
bear_points: [E] The reverse DCF implies about 70% annual sales growth for five years against an 8.3% base-case equivalent; the bear, base and bull values (Rs 65 / 109 / 145) are 78-90% below the Rs 665 price (NUMBERS).
[F] Sales grew only 3.8% a year over three years and standalone volume fell 5.9% year on year in Q1FY27; CFO/PAT was 0.51x in FY26 and FCF was negative (NUMBERS; PPT Jul 2026).
[E] Excluding the Rs 100 cr fair-value gain on unlisted investments and the tax-regime switch (effective rate 31.1% to 24.6%), FY26 PAT growth would be about 11%, not 36% (AR2026 p.490, p.494).

[F] Rs 486.5 cr is held in 0.001% NCDs of Dalmia Bharat Refractories, the partner holding Birla Tyres manufacturing, and Rs 182.6 cr in 1% OCPS of promoter holding company Modern Hi-Rise (AR2026 p.468-469).

[MC] LFP Phase 1 went from 40,000 MTPA operational by Q3FY27 (Oct 2025) to a 2,000 MTPA demo line by Q3FY27, with 40,000 MTPA in FY28 and full operations in FY29; no offtake is disclosed (CALL Oct 2025; CALL Jul 2026).
